choice.stem: 다음 요약문의 빈칸 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
choice.ex: (A) influential (B) modeling (C) direct 근거 ❷❸❺❻ 해설: (A) ❷ gain in importance → influential (important도 성립, irrelevant·predictable·harmful은 오류) / (B) ❸ serve as a role model → modeling (demonstrating도 성립, hiding·scolding·ignoring은 반대) / (C) ❺ direct soothing and directive guidance → direct (hands-on·directive도 성립, indirect는 청소년에게 맞는 쪽이라 반대, delayed는 무관). 요약문 해석: 청소년기에 또래와 미디어가 더 (A) 영향력 있어지지만, 부모는 여전히 자녀가 감정을 다루는 방식을 형성하는데, 부분적으로는 자녀가 나중 에 따라 하는 침착한 반응을 (B) 본보여 줌으로써이다. 그러나 어린아이에게 맞는 (C) 직접적인 도움은 십 대에게는 역효과를 낼 수 있다.
choice.psg: ❶ Emotion socialization — learning from other people about emotions and how to deal with them — starts early in life and plays a foundational role for emotion regulation development. ❷ Although extra-familial influences, such as peers or media, gain in importance during adolescence, parents remain the primary socialization agents. ❸ For example, their own responses to emotional situations serve as a role model for emotion regulation, increasing the likelihood that their children will show similar reactions in comparable situations. ❹ Parental practices at times when their children are faced with emotional challenges also impact emotion regulation development. ❺ Whereas direct soothing and directive guidance of what to do are beneficial for younger children, they may intrude on adolescents’ autonomy striving. ❻ In consequence, adolescents might pull away from, rather than turn toward, their parents in times of emotional crisis, unless parental practices are adjusted. ❼ More suitable in adolescence is indirect support of autonomous emotion regulation, such as through interest in, as well as awareness and nonjudgmental acceptance of, adolescents’ emotional experiences, and being available when the adolescent wants to talk.
choice.body: Although peers and media grow more (A)________ in adolescence, parents still shape how their children manage emotions, partly by (B)________ calm responses that children later copy; however, the (C)________ help that suits young children may backfire with teenagers.

choice.stem: 다음 요약문의 빈칸 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
choice.ex: (A) value (B) drive (C) subtle 근거 ❺❻❼ 해설: (A) ❺ autonomy striving → value (seek·prize도 성립, reject·fear는 반대) / (B) ❻ pull away from → drive away (push도 성립, summon·retain·invite는 반대) / (C) ❼ indirect support → subtle (quiet도 성립, strict·constant는 ❺의 개입 쪽, financial은 무관). 요약문 해석: 청소년은 독립을 (A) 소중히 여기기 때문에, 직접적인 지시를 계속하는 부모는 정서적 위기에서 그들을 (B) 밀어낼 수 있다. 대신 부모는 관 심을 보이고 곁에 있어 줌으로써 (C) 은근한 지원을 제공해야 한다.

growing influence of peers and media
parental reactions as examples for children

choice.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분이 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
opt: Teenagers need even more explicit instructions from parents than younger children do in emotional situations.
Teenagers may feel that constant comfort and instructions interfere with their wish to handle things alone.
Younger children feel more pressure from parental guidance than teenagers do in times of crisis.
Teenagers ignore their parents’ advice mainly because they want to make their parents feel guilty.
Teenagers reject every form of parental help and even refuse simple interest in their emotional lives.
choice.ex: 밑줄 해석: 직접적인 위로와 어떻게 해야 하는지에 대한 지시적 안내가 어린 자녀에게는 도움이 되지만, 청소년의 자율성 추구를 방해 할 수 있다. 해설: ‘청소년의 자율성 추구를 방해한다’ = 어린아이에게 좋은 직접적 위로·지시가 스스로 하려는 십 대의 바람을 침해함 — 뒤 ❻ 부모에게서 멀어짐으로 이어짐. ① 십 대는 감정적 상황에서 어린아이보다 부모의 훨씬 더 상세한 지시가 필요하다. 오답 — 방향 뒤집기(더 많은 지시 필요) ② 십 대는 끊임없는 위로와 지시가 스스로 일을 처리하려는 바람을 방해한다고 느낄 수 있다. 정답 ③ 어린아이들이 위기 때 십 대보다 부모의 지도에서 더 큰 압박을 느낀다. 오답 — 주체 바꿔치기(어린아이가 압박) ④ 십 대는 주로 부모가 죄책감을 느끼게 하고 싶어서 부모의 조언을 무시한다. 오답 — 의도 심기(죄책감) ⑤ 십 대는 모든 형태의 부모 도움을 거부하고 자신의 감정생활에 대한 단순한 관심조차 거절한다. 오답 — 범위 확대(모든 도움 거부)
choice.body: Parental practices at times when their children are faced with emotional challenges also impact emotion regulation development. Whereas direct soothing and directive guidance of what to do are beneficial for younger children, they may intrude on adolescents’ autonomy striving. In consequence, adolescents might pull away from, rather than turn toward, their parents in times of emotional crisis, unless parental practices are adjusted.

choice.stem: 다음 요약문의 빈칸 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
choice.ex: (A) disastrous (B) inactive (C) generated 근거 ❷❸❻❼❽ 해설: (A) ❸ 경제가 유지되리라 믿기 어려움 → disastrous (catastrophic도 성립, harmless·beneficial·ordinary는 반대) / (B) ❼ did not sit idle → inactive (unemployed·jobless도 성립, busy·wealthy는 문맥상 ‘머물지 않았다’와 모순) / (C) ❽ automation created → generated (produced도 성 립, eliminated·hid·copied는 오류). 요약문 해석: 대부분의 농장 일자리를 기계에 빼앗기는 것은 (A) 재앙처럼 들리지만, 일자리를 잃은 노동자들은 (B) 무위로 머물지 않았다. 자동화가 대신 이전에 없던 분야에서 수많은 일자리를 (C) 만들어 냈다.
choice.psg: ❶ Imagine that seven out of ten working Americans got fired tomorrow. ❷ What would they all do? ❸ It’s hard to believe you’d have an economy at all if you gave pink slips to more than half the labor force. ❹ But that is what the industrial revolution did to the workforce of the early 19th century. ❺ Two hundred years ago, 70 percent of American workers lived on the farm. ❻ Today automation has eliminated all but 1 percent of their jobs, replacing them with machines. ❼ But the displaced workers did not sit idle. ❽ Instead, automation created hundreds of millions of jobs in entirely new fields. ❾ Those who once farmed were now manning the factories that manufactured farm equipment, cars, and other industrial products. ❿ Since then, wave upon wave of new occupations have arrived — appliance repair person, food chemist, photographer, web designer — each building on previous automation. ⓫ Today, the vast majority of us are doing jobs that no farmer from the 1800s could have imagined.
choice.body: Although losing most farm jobs to machines sounds (A)________, the workers who were displaced did not stay (B)________; automation instead (C)________ countless jobs in fields that did not exist before.

choice.stem: 다음 요약문의 빈칸 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
choice.ex: (A) built (B) novel (C) unimaginable 근거 ❿⓫ 해설: (A) ❿ each building on previous automation → built on (drawn on도 성립, frowned·turned·spied on은 뜻이 어긋남) / (B) ❿ new occupations → novel (unfamiliar·unprecedented도 성립, traditional·simple은 반대) / (C) ⓫ could have imagined의 부정 → unimaginable (inconceivable도 성립, obvious·tedious·available은 오류). 요약문 해석: 자동화의 각 물결은 이전의 것들을 (A) 기반으로 삼아, 너무나 (B) 새로운 직업들을 만들어 내서 오늘날 일자리의 대부분은 1800년대 농부 들에게 (C) 상상할 수 없는 것이었을 것이다.

choice.body: Each wave of automation has (A)________ on earlier ones, creating occupations so (B)________ that most of today’s jobs would have been (C)________ to farmers of the 1800s.

choice.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분이 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.

choice.body: Today automation has eliminated all but 1 percent of their jobs, replacing them with machines. But the displaced workers did not sit idle. Instead, automation created hundreds of millions of jobs in entirely new fields.
choice.ul: the displaced workers did not sit idle.

choice.stem: 다음 요약문의 빈칸 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
choice.ex: (A) rigorous (B) predictable (C) centuries 근거 ❷❹❺ 해설: (A) ❷ precise, mathematical and statistical → rigorous (quantitative·systematic도 성립, haphazard·emotional은 반대) / (B) ❹❺ profoundly regular, periodic cycle → predictable (cyclical도 성립, random·chaotic·sudden은 반대) / (C) ❹ on the scale of history, not annual → centuries (generations도 성립, weeks·months·seasons는 annual보다도 짧음). 요약문 해석: 옛 이미지를 표준화하고 몇 가지 의류 특징을 측정함으로써, Kroeber는 여성 패션이 해마다가 아니라 (C) 수 세기에 걸쳐 볼 때 (B) 예측 가 능한 방식으로 변한다는 것을 보여 주는 (A) 엄밀한 분석을 내놓았다.
choice.psg: ❶ The well-known American ethnologist Alfred Louis Kroeber made a rich and in-depth study of women’s evening dress in the West, stretching back about three centuries and using reproductions of engravings. ❷ Having adjusted the dimensions of these plates due to their diverse origins, he was able to analyse the constant elements in fashion features and to come up with a study that was neither intuitive nor approximate, but precise, mathematical and statistical. ❸ He reduced women’s clothing to a certain number of features: length and size of the skirt, size and depth of the neckline, height of the waistline. ❹ He demonstrated unambiguously that fashion is a profoundly regular phenomenon which is not located at the level of annual variations but on the scale of history. ❺ For practically 300 years, women’s dress was subject to a very precise periodic cycle: forms reach the furthest point in their variations every fifty years. ❻ If, at any one moment, skirts are at their longest, fifty years later they will be at their shortest; thus skirts become long again fifty years after being short and a hundred years after being long.
choice.body: By standardizing old images and measuring a few clothing features, Kroeber produced a (A)________ analysis showing that women’s fashion changes in a (B)________ way when viewed over (C)________ rather than year by year.

choice.stem: 다음 요약문의 빈칸 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
choice.ex: (A) extreme (B) returned (C) century 근거 ❺❻ 해설: (A) ❺ the furthest point in their variations → extreme (peak·limit도 성립, average·origin은 오류) / (B) ❻ become long again → returned (reverted도 성립, refused·migrated·shrank는 오류) / (C) ❻ a hundred years after being long → century (cycle도 성립, decade·season·year 는 길이가 맞지 않음). 요약문 해석: 여성 이브닝드레스는 각 특징이 약 50년마다 (A) 극단에 이르는 규칙적 순환을 따라서, 어느 시점에 길었던 스커트는 반세기 뒤에 짧아졌다 가 꼬박 (C) 한 세기가 지나면 원래 길이로 (B) 돌아왔다.

choice.psg: ❶ Some people argue that there is a single, logically consistent concept known as reading that can be neatly set apart from everything else people do with books. ❷ Is reading really that simple? ❸ The most productive way to think about reading is as a loosely related set of behaviors that belong together owing to family resemblances, as Ludwig Wittgenstein used the phrase, without having in common a single defining trait. ❹ Consequently, efforts to distinguish reading from nonreading are destined to fail because there is no agreement on what qualifies as reading in the first place. ❺ The more one tries to figure out where the border lies between reading and not-reading, the more edge cases will be found to stretch the term’s flexible boundaries. ❻ Thus, it is worth attempting to collect together these exceptional forms of reading into a single forum, one highlighting the challenges faced by anyone wishing to establish the boundaries where reading begins and ends. ❼ The attempt moves toward an understanding of reading as a spectrum that is expansive enough to accommodate the distinct reading activities.
choice.body: Reading cannot be (A)________ by a single defining feature; instead, it is better understood as a group of activities linked by (B)________ similarities, which is why attempts to draw a clear line around it (C)________ fail.

order.A: For example, their own responses to emotional situations serve as a role model for emotion regulation, increasing the likelihood that their children will show similar reactions in comparable situations. Parental practices at times when their children are faced with emotional challenges also impact emotion regulation development.
order.B: Emotion socialization — learning from other people about emotions and how to deal with them — starts early in life and plays a foundational role for emotion regulation development. Although extra-familial influences, such as peers or media, gain in importance during adolescence, parents remain the primary socialization agents.
order.C: Whereas direct soothing and directive guidance of what to do are beneficial for younger children, they may intrude on adolescents’ autonomy striving. read.ko: 하지만 그것은 19세기 초 노동력에 산업혁명이 했던 것이다.
read.en: But that is what the industrial revolution did to the workforce of the early 19th century.

read.ko: 200년 전, 미국 노동자의 70%가 농장에서 살았다.
read.en: Two hundred years ago, 70 percent of American workers lived on the farm.

read.ko: 오늘날 자동화는 1%를 제외한 모든 일자리를 제거하였고, 그것들을 기계로 대체하였다.
read.en: Today automation has eliminated all but 1 percent of their jobs, replacing them with machines.

read.ko: 하지만 일자리를 잃은 노동자들은 한가롭게 앉아 있지 않았다.
read.en: But the displaced workers did not sit idle.

read.ko: 그 대신, 자동화는 완전히 새로운 분야에서 수억 개의 일자리를 창출했다.
read.en: Instead, automation created hundreds of millions of jobs in entirely new fields.

read.ko: 한때 농사를 짓던 사람들은 이제 농기구, 자동차, 그리고 기타 산업 제품을 제조하는 공장에서 일하고 있다.
read.en: Those who once farmed were now manning the factories that manufactured farm equipment, cars, and other industrial products.

read.ko: 그 이후로, 가전제품 수리공, 식품 화학자, 사진작가, 웹 디자이너 등 이전의 자동화를 기반으로 한 새로운 직업이 계속해서 등장했다.
read.en: Since then, wave upon wave of new occupations have arrived — appliance repair person, food chemist, photographer, web designer — each building on previous automation.

read.ko: 오늘날, 우리 중 대다수는 1800년대의 농부들은 상상도 할 수 없었던 일을 하고 있다.
read.en: Today, the vast majority of us are doing jobs that no farmer from the 1800s could have imagined.

read.ko: 미국의 잘 알려진 민속학자인 Alfred Louis Kroeber는 약 3세기 전으로 거슬러 올라가 판화 복제품을 사용하여 서양의 여성 이브닝 드레스에 대한 풍부 하고 심도 있는 연구를 수행했다.
read.en: The well-known American ethnologist Alfred Louis Kroeber made a rich and in-depth study of women’s evening dress in the West, stretching back about three centuries and using reproductions of engravings.

read.ko: 다양한 기원 때문에 이 판들의 크기를 조정하여, 그는 패션 특징에서의 일정한 요소를 분석해서 직관적이지도 대략적이지도 않은, 정확하고 수학적이며 통 계적인 연구를 구상할 수 있었다.
read.en: Having adjusted the dimensions of these plates due to their diverse origins, he was able to analyse the constant elements in fashion features and to come up with a study that was neither intuitive nor approximate, but precise, mathematical and statistical.

read.ko: 그는 여성 의류를 스커트의 길이와 크기, 목선의 크기와 깊이, 허리선의 높이와 같은 몇 가지 특징들로 정리했다.
read.en: He reduced women’s clothing to a certain number of features: length and size of the skirt, size and depth of the neckline, height of the waistline.

read.ko: 그는 패션이 매년 일어나는 변화의 수준이 아니라 역사의 척도에 위치하는 매우 규칙적인 현상이라는 것을 분명하게 보여주었다.
read.en: He demonstrated unambiguously that fashion is a profoundly regular phenomenon which is not located at the level of annual variations but on the scale of history.

read.ko: 거의 300년 동안 여성 드레스는 매우 정확한 주기적인 순환의 영향을 받았는데, 형식은 50년마다 변화의 정점에 도달했다.
read.en: For practically 300 years, women’s dress was subject to a very precise periodic cycle: forms reach the furthest point in their variations every fifty years.

read.ko: 어느 한 시기에 스커트가 가장 길었다면 50년 후에 가장 짧아질 것이고, 따라서 스커트는 짧아진 데서 50년 후에 다시 길어지고, 길어진 데서 100년 후에 길어진다.
read.en: If, at any one moment, skirts are at their longest, fifty years later they will be at their shortest; thus skirts become long again fifty years after being short and a hundred years after being long.

read.ko: 몇몇 사람들은 사람들이 책을 가지고 하는 모든 다른 행동들로부터 깔끔하게 분리될 수 있는, 읽기로 알려진 유일하고 논리적으로 일관성 있는 개념이 있 다고 주장한다.
read.en: Some people argue that there is a single, logically consistent concept known as reading that can be neatly set apart from everything else people do with books.

read.ko: 읽기는 정말로 그렇게 단순할까?
read.en: Is reading really that simple?

read.ko: 읽기에 대해 생각하는 가장 생산적인 방식은 하나의 명백한 특성을 공통적으로 가지지 않은 채 Ludwig Wittgenstein이 그 어구를 사용한 것처럼 가족 유 사성 때문에 함께 속하게 되는 헐겁게 연결된 행동의 묶음으로서이다.
read.en: The most productive way to think about reading is as a loosely related set of behaviors that belong together owing to family resemblances, as Ludwig Wittgenstein used the phrase, without having in common a single defining trait.

read.ko: 결론적으로, 읽기와 읽기가 아닌 것을 구분하려는 노력은 실패로 돌아가는데, 왜냐하면 애초에 무엇이 읽기로서의 자격을 주는가에 대한 동의가 없기 때문 이다.
read.en: Consequently, efforts to distinguish reading from nonreading are destined to fail because there is no agreement on what qualifies as reading in the first place.

read.ko: 읽기와 읽기가 아닌 것 사이의 경계가 어디에 있는가를 알려고 하면 할수록, 더욱 많은 특이 사례들이 그 용어의 유연한 경계를 확장하고 있다는 것이 밝혀 질 것이다.
read.en: The more one tries to figure out where the border lies between reading and not-reading, the more edge cases will be found to stretch the term’s flexible boundaries.

read.ko: 그러므로, 이러한 예외적인 읽기의 형태들을 모두 함께 하나의 토론의 장으로 모으려는 시도는 해 볼 가치가 있으며, 그 토론의 장은 어디서 읽기가 시작되 고 끝나는가에 대한 경계를 정하기를 원하는 누구나에 의해 마주하게 될 어려움들을 돋보이게 한다.
read.en: Thus, it is worth attempting to collect together these exceptional forms of reading into a single forum, one highlighting the challenges faced by anyone wishing to establish the boundaries where reading begins and ends.

read.ko: 그러한 시도는 별개의 읽기 활동들을 다 수용할 만큼 충분히 광범위한 스펙트럼으로서 읽기를 이해하는 것으로 발전한다.
read.en: The attempt moves toward an understanding of reading as a spectrum that is expansive enough to accommodate the distinct reading activities.

read.ko: 이론적으로는 우리의 뇌는 DVD의 품질에 도달할 정도로, 삶의 모든 경험들을 저장할 수 있는 수용력을 가지고 있을 것이다.
read.en: Theoretically, our brain would have the capacity to store all experiences throughout life, reaching the quality of a DVD.

read.ko: 그러나, 이 이론상의 수용력은 기억에 정보를 저장하고 상기하는 과정과 관련된 에너지 수요로 인해 상쇄된다.
read.en: However, this theoretical capacity is offset by the energy demand associated with the process of storing and retrieving information in memory.

read.ko: 그 결과, 뇌는 효율적인 전략들을 수립하고, 지름길에 의존하게 된다.
read.en: As a result, the brain develops efficient strategies, becoming dependent on shortcuts.

read.ko: 우리가 얼굴을 관찰할 때, 눈에 의해 포착되는 시각적 이미지는 시점, 조명 조건 및 기타 상황적 요인들에 따라 매우 다양하다.
read.en: When we observe a face, the visual image captured by the eyes is highly variable, depending on the point of view, lighting conditions and other contextual factors.

read.ko: 그럼에도 불구하고, 우리는 근본적인 정체성을 유지하면서 얼굴을 같은 것으로 인식할 수 있다.
read.en: Nevertheless, we are able to recognize the face as the same, maintaining the underlying identity.

read.ko: 뇌는 시각화의 세부 사항에 집중하기보다 다양한 상황들에서 일관된 인식을 가능하게 하는 일반적인 패턴을 생성하고 저장한다.
read.en: The brain, rather than focusing on the details of visualization, creates and stores general patterns that allow for consistent recognition across diverse circumstances.

read.ko: 우리가 보는 것과 일반적인 시각 기억 패턴을 일치시키는 이 능력은 뇌의 수행을 최적화하고 에너지를 절약하는 효과적인 기제로 작용한다.
read.en: This ability to match what we see with general visual memory patterns serves as an effective mechanism for optimizing brain performance and saving energy.

read.ko: 불필요한 노력에 자연스럽게 대항하는 뇌는 인지 과정을 돕기 위해서 끊임없이 정보를 단순화하고 일반화하는 것을 추구한다.
read.en: The brain, being naturally against unnecessary effort, constantly seeks to simplify and generalize information to facilitate the cognitive process.

para.en: Emotion socialization — learning from other people about emotions and how to deal with them — starts early in life and plays a foundational role for emotion regulation development. Although extra-familial influences, such as peers or media, gain in importance during adolescence, parents remain the primary socialization agents. For example, their own responses to emotional situations serve as a role model for emotion regulation, increasing the likelihood that their children will show similar reactions in comparable situations. Parental practices at times when their children are faced with emotional challenges also impact emotion regulation development. Whereas direct soothing and directive guidance of what to do are beneficial for younger children, they may intrude on adolescents’ autonomy striving. In consequence, adolescents might pull away from, rather than turn toward, their parents in times of emotional crisis, unless parental practices are adjusted. More suitable in adolescence is indirect support of autonomous emotion regulation, such as through interest in, as well as awareness and nonjudgmental acceptance of, adolescents’ emotional experiences, and being available when the adolescent wants to talk.

Imagine that seven out of ten working Americans got fired tomorrow. What would they all do? It’s hard to believe you’d have an economy at all if you gave pink slips to more than half the labor force. But that is what the industrial revolution did to the workforce of the early 19th century. Two hundred years ago, 70 percent of American workers lived on the farm. Today automation has eliminated all but 1 percent of their jobs, replacing them with machines. But the displaced workers did not sit idle. Instead, automation created hundreds of millions of jobs in entirely new fields. Those who once farmed were now manning the factories that manufactured farm equipment, cars, and other industrial products. Since then, wave upon wave of new occupations have arrived — appliance repair person, food chemist, photographer, web designer — each building on previous automation. Today, the vast majority of us are doing jobs that no farmer from the 1800s could have imagined.

The well-known American ethnologist Alfred Louis Kroeber made a rich and in-depth study of women’s evening dress in the West, stretching back about three centuries and using reproductions of engravings. Having adjusted the dimensions of these plates due to their diverse origins, he was able to analyse the constant elements in fashion features and to come up with a study that was neither intuitive nor approximate, but precise, mathematical and statistical. He reduced women’s clothing to a certain number of features: length and size of the skirt, size and depth of the neckline, height of the waistline. He demonstrated unambiguously that fashion is a profoundly regular phenomenon which is not located at the level of annual variations but on the scale of history. For practically 300 years, women’s dress was subject to a very precise periodic cycle: forms reach the furthest point in their variations every fifty years. If, at any one moment, skirts are at their longest, fifty years later they will be at their shortest; thus skirts become long again fifty years after being short and a hundred years after being long.

Some people argue that there is a single, logically consistent concept known as reading that can be neatly set apart from everything else people do with books. Is reading really that simple? The most productive way to think about reading is as a loosely related set of behaviors that belong together owing to family resemblances, as Ludwig Wittgenstein used the phrase, without having in common a single defining trait. Consequently, efforts to distinguish reading from nonreading are destined to fail because there is no agreement on what qualifies as reading in the first place. The more one tries to figure out where the border lies between reading and not-reading, the more edge cases will be found to stretch the term’s flexible boundaries. Thus, it is worth attempting to collect together these exceptional forms of reading into a single forum, one highlighting the challenges faced by anyone wishing to establish the boundaries where reading begins and ends. The attempt moves toward an understanding of reading as a spectrum that is expansive enough to accommodate the distinct reading activities.

Theoretically, our brain would have the capacity to store all experiences throughout life, reaching the quality of a DVD. However, this theoretical capacity is offset by the energy demand associated with the process of storing and retrieving information in memory. As a result, the brain develops efficient strategies, becoming dependent on shortcuts. When we observe a face, the visual image captured by the eyes is highly variable, depending on the point of view, lighting conditions and other contextual factors. Nevertheless, we are able to recognize the face as the same, maintaining the underlying identity. The brain, rather than focusing on the details of visualization, creates and stores general patterns that allow for consistent recognition across diverse circumstances. This ability to match what we see with general visual memory patterns serves as an effective mechanism for optimizing brain performance and saving energy. The brain, being naturally against unnecessary effort, constantly seeks to simplify and generalize information to facilitate the cognitive process.
